The correction preserves `RIB_SEGMENTS`, rendered geometry, canonical `SOLIDS` rib AABBs, `WorldQueries`, `Capsule`, `MoveResult`, and every exported world-function signature. `createWorldQueries`, `hullFloor`, `hullClearance`, `moveHull`, and `sweptHullClearance` retain their interfaces. The old optical registration map is reused as `CANONICAL_RIBS`; both ID and all six bounds must equal the canonical record. Detached canonical clones receive curved physics. Empty/filtered rosters acquire no omitted global ribs; a reused rib ID with changed bounds stays an ordinary solid. There is no new query argument, public actor-shape API, actor inference, or additional hidden registry.

Actors retain their full fixed-axis boxes: X ±(`halfWidth ?? radius`), Z ±(`halfLength ?? radius`), Y +[`bottom ?? 0`, `height`]. The internal helper exports `BoxBounds`, `actorBox`, `sweptBoxIntersects`, `segmentBoxClosest`, `RibSweepHit`, `sweepBoxRib`, `ribUpperHeight`, and four numerical constants solely for world integration/regression access. No types, step, vehicles, carrier, registry, save, art, CSS, UI, encounter tuning, velocity, acceleration, fixed tick, yields, board/exit rules, or migration code changed.

`segmentBoxClosest` computes the exact minimum distance from the full segment axis to the full actor AABB in real arithmetic. Segment crossings of the six box slabs partition [0,1] into at most seven pieces. Squared point/box distance is quadratic on each piece; evaluating its endpoints and clamped stationary point gives the global minimum. The closest pair supplies a normal from the rib axis toward the actor. Zero-length segments, zero-size boxes/points, interior intersections, parallel and non-cardinal axes are supported. Static collision compares that distance with the capsule radius. LOS retains its prior segment-to-segment capsule test, including strict tangency and ignore-list behavior.

`sweepBoxRib` continuously advances the translating box against one convex segment capsule. At current closest separation `d` and outward unit normal `n`, `d + n·delta·dt` is a supporting-plane lower bound on future axis/box distance. A positive closing projection therefore permits an advance of `(d-radius)/(-n·delta)` without passing first contact. A nonclosing separating plane, or an advance beyond the remaining interval, proves that straight remainder clear. This is a continuous geometric sweep; fixed spatial samples and endpoint overlap are not its proof.

| Bound / tolerance | Exact behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Static/initial overlap tolerance | **0.001 m**, retaining the legacy clearance tolerance. `distance < radius - .001` is invalid overlap. |
| New sweep contact band | **0.000001 m** separation; an approaching box at or below this gap returns contact. |
| Numerical tangent | An inward projection of at most **1e-12 m over the entire displacement**, with nonnegative gap, is treated as tangent. |
| Advancement budget | **64** exact distance evaluations per candidate rib. Production always uses 64; a lower internal test budget exercises exhaustion. |
| Slide budget | **8** contact iterations per world movement. Every resulting tangent is swept against the entire supplied solid roster again. |
| Remaining-displacement cutoff | Norm below **1e-12 m** terminates movement. |
| Ordinary AABB backoff | Existing fractional **0.0001** backoff is retained for unrelated solids; ribs use their geometric contact position. |

World movement selects the earliest returned contact across all candidates. It subtracts only the inward component `n * min(remaining·n, 0)` from the remaining displacement; it does not zero all axes touched by a curved normal. Deep initial overlap returns the original pose with `hitSolid`, without teleporting. Invalid deltas/shapes fail closed; a nonfinite origin throws `RangeError`. Unrepresentable distance, advancement no-progress, or advancement exhaustion returns `stop:true`, discarding unproved travel. Eight unresolved slides also discard the remainder. The regression suite forces advancement exhaustion, and the stress receipt observes actual slide-budget termination. These outcomes are conservative stops, not clear travel.

The sweep proof uses convexity and real arithmetic. The implementation uses IEEE doubles and the explicit separation/projection tolerances above; it is not a formal interval-arithmetic proof. Grazing contact has a spatial tolerance and no uniform time-error bound. Exhaustion can stop early. A tangent at one contact can meet a different rib/solid and is checked again. Terrain/hull-footprint sampling and existing boundary handling remain unchanged; this correction does not claim continuous terrain collision.

`clearance` uses the same full-box geometry and 1 mm overlap tolerance. Sweeps from clear space stop outside the true surface within the 1 µm band; tolerance-accepted legacy poses can stay put or leave. A radius-reduced capsule is contained in the old registration AABB reduced by the same 1 mm on each face. Every previously clear valid legacy pose therefore remains clear under the new static predicate. No save migration or relocation is needed. Future movement that actually touches a corrected rib can differ.

`supportHeight` analytically computes the upper intersection of a vertical line at queried X/Z with the capsule, including segment end spheres. It maximizes `ay+uy*s+sqrt(radius²-horizontalDistance(s)²)` over its feasible segment interval using the concave stationary point and interval endpoints. It retains `fromY >= upper - .25`, floor support and supplied `floorHeight`. Empty parts of the registration AABB no longer provide an invisible flat roof.

Timings use unmodified compiled modules; call counts use separate temporary instrumentation. They measure `moveCapsule`, not rendering or whole-game frame time:

| Route / displacement | Median µs per call | Exact distance calls | Rib sweeps / maximum advancement evaluations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No-rib swimmer, .08 m | 1.22 | 0 | 0 / 0 |
| No-rib ordinary shallow Dart, .14 m | 1.27 | 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Exact B rise, .3 m | 5.01 | 1 | 1 / 1 |
| All-axis endcap glance | 10.03 | 5 | 2 / 4 |
| Rib crossing, 24 m | 29.75 | 16 | 6 / 8 |

The default roster has 62 broadphase candidates per pass. The theoretical default-roster rib bound is **36 ribs × 8 slides × 64 evaluations = 18,432 distance calls per movement**; local caller-provided roster size scales that bound. A fixed-seed 10,000-candidate stress run accepted 9,250 initially clear poses, produced 1,606 contacts, and retained clear final poses for all. Its observed maximum was 11 advancement evaluations and 8 slides. [Additional budget instrumentation](/tmp/siltwake-polish-1-slice2-rib/slide-budget.json) observed **two actual eighth-contact stops**, preserving clear final poses while discarding unresolved remainders; it records the first exact fixture. Stress uses supplied floor −200 m to isolate solids, because raw `moveCapsule` terrain correction remains a caller responsibility. An initial diagnostic harness mistakenly checked raw movement against default terrain; that harness assertion was corrected without changing production code. These bounded CPU observations are not a GPU claim or a guarantee for every possible query.
